articles.title: Why Arturo Béjar left Meta – and blew the whistle: ‘I don’t recall Mark ever being empathetic’
articles.summary: Béjar’s daughter was 14 when she told him Instagram was failing to keep her safe. So when he became part of Meta’s ‘wellbeing team’, he knew he had to speak out – and his testimony cost it billions.
body: The Social Reckoning hits cinemas this Friday, but the real world has already been working on a sequel – or rather, a threequel. Directed by Aaron Sorkin, the movie is a follow-up to The Social Network, detailing the further misadventures of Mark Zuckerberg and his social media empire, and in particular Frances Haugen, the employee who in 2021 leaked internal documents that appeared to show Facebook was aware of the harms its products had inflicted.

By that time, Béjar had worked at Facebook (which rebranded as Meta later that month) for a total of eight years. He had learned how to communicate with Zuckerberg. “You couldn’t talk to Mark about, ‘We have to do this thing to prevent suicide because it’s the right thing to do,’” he says. “You had to put everything in terms of metrics. That was his language. That’s how he related to things, which is also what’s behind all the grief in the world right now.”
points: Béjar’s daughter was 14 when she told him Instagram was failing to keep her safe.
So when he became part of Meta’s ‘wellbeing team’, he knew he had to speak out – and his testimony cost it billions.

articles.title: Wim Wenders Boards Peter Lindbergh Documentary ‘Truth:Beauty’
articles.summary: Wim Wenders has boarded “Truth:Beauty,” a feature documentary about legendary German fashion photographer Peter Lindbergh, as executive producer. The project, produced by Maja Hoffmann and Human Humans, will mark the feature directorial debut of French novelist Alexandra Matine, whose books include…
body: Principal photography on “Truth:Beauty” is expected to kick off before the end of the year.

One of the most influential fashion photographers of his generation, Lindbergh, who died in 2019 at the age of 74, helped usher in the era of the supermodel with his striking black-and-white portraits. Over a career spanning four decades, he became known for bringing a more natural and realistic approach to fashion photography, moving away from the heavily stylized images that had dominated the industry.

Wenders and Lindbergh, who belonged to the same generation of German artists, shared a friendship spanning several decades. Their work also influenced one another. Lindbergh’s 1993 Harper’s Bazaar editorial “City of Angels” was directly inspired by Wenders’ “Wings of Desire.”

One of Germany’s most celebrated filmmakers, Wenders won the Palme d’Or at Cannes for “Paris, Texas,” the Golden Lion at Venice for “The State of Things,” and the best director prize at Cannes for “Wings of Desire.” He has also earned four Oscar nominations, including three in the documentary feature category for “Buena Vista Social Club,” “Pina” and “The Salt of the Earth.”

articles.title: Charlotte Gainsbourg on Listening to ‘Controversial’ Kanye West and Working With ‘Tortured’ Lars von Trier at Busan
articles.summary: Charlotte Gainsbourg had one artist to recommend to the crowd at her Busan International Film Festival masterclass, and it was not a safe pick. “I’m not good for recommendation.
body: “I’m not good for recommendation. I have one artist that I listen to, very controversial artist, but I listen to everything he does, and it’s Kanye West,” Gainsbourg said, to laughter from the audience. “I know, it’s very easy.”
“I guess it was the easiest choice, ‘Melancholia,’ and also because selfishly, I want to see it again,” Gainsbourg said, laughing. “I haven’t seen it in 15 years.”
The screening followed straight after the session, and the moderator warned the audience they would lose about five minutes so Gainsbourg could catch it.
Then the conversation turned to von Trier himself. “Well, I can’t say he’s a friend, but he’s a dear friend,” she said. “I don’t know him that well, but we exchange text messages.”

articles.title: Louis Garrel to Play Fiat Heir John Elkann in Marco Bellocchio’s ‘Falcon’; RAI Cinema International Boards for Sales
articles.summary: Louis Garrel is set to play John Elkann — heir to Italy’s Agnelli family, behind car giant Fiat — in Italian auteur Marco Bellocchio’s “Falcon.” The biopic centers on charismatic auto industry executive Sergio Marchionne, played by Pierfrancesco Favino, who saved Fiat from the brink of bankruptcy.
body: “Ruthless and visionary, he axes the top management, teaches John Elkann (Garrel), the young heir suddenly burdened with the family’s legacy, the art of command, and conquers the American market by fighting General Motors and Chrysler, saving FIAT from bankruptcy,” the film’s synopsis says.

Then, in 2009, when Chrysler was guided into a U.S. government-led bankruptcy, Marchionne offered to take control of the company essentially for free. With no other option, the U.S. Treasury Department accepted his offer. By merging the two failing car companies, Marchionne created the seventh-largest vehicle manufacturer in the world, increasing Fiat’s value more than tenfold.

“Marchionne became very important and famous overseas,” promotional materials note. “But the miracle exacted a devastating price. Blending the razor-sharp tension of a financial thriller with deep psychological insight, ‘Falcon’ explores the heights of capitalism and the fatal, profound isolation of a tragic victor swallowed by the very machine he saved.”

articles.title: Alfonso Cuaron Revisits ‘Gravity’ With Son Jonas at Busan: ‘Life as an Experience Is What I Now Care About the Most’
articles.summary: When he was younger, film came first for Alfonso Cuarón. These days, the Oscar-winning director says, life does. He made the remark at his Busan International Film Festival masterclass on Thursday, a day after he and his son Jonas Cuaron, his co-writer on 2013 space survival drama “Gravity,”…
body: When he was younger, film came first for Alfonso Cuarón. These days, the Oscar-winning director says, life does.

For Jonas, “Gravity’s” core was rebirth: two characters confronting loss and finding a way forward, with limited dialogue and an environment that made every action matter. Alfonso recalled their discussions about how setting and movement could express the desire to survive.

Their collaboration also drew on the films they watched together. At a press conference, Alfonso remembered Jonas’ childhood affection for Robert Bresson’s “A Man Escaped” and Vittorio De Sica’s “Bicycle Thieves.”
“Growing up watching movies that he loves, and then discovering what I love, I tend to tell a story that is simple but powerful in terms of emotions,” Jonás said.

articles.title: Big Girls Don’t Cry review – a New Zealand teenager finds herself in tender coming-of-age tale
articles.summary: Writer-director Paloma Schneideman’s wonderful film follows a 14-year-old in 2006 who pretends to be someone else in a chat room, with real-world consequences. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: A ll coming-of-age films face the challenge of how to convey that intermediary period between childhood and adulthood, with all the confusion, awkwardness and self-searching that entails. Writer-director Paloma Schneideman’s drama Big Girls Don’t Cry meets that challenge, resulting in a tenderly drawn story about the slow process of a 14-year-old in rural New Zealand finding herself.

The best coming-of-age stories tend to follow rebellious characters (like Antoine Doinel in The 400 Blows and Jim Stark in Rebel Without a Cause ), outsiders (like Mia Williams in Fish Tank and Sybylla Melvyn in My Brilliant Career ), or the more experimental and vulnerable kind (like Heidi in Somersault and Lidia in Kristen Stewart’s magnificent directorial debut The Chronology of Water ).
Now there’s Sid (Ani Palmer), who is a difficult person to categorise. She’s a bit of an introvert, a bit of a tough nut to crack: rarely outwardly friendly, but not exactly standoffish either.

articles.title: Paul McCartney's key sells for double the estimate
articles.summary: The star composed some of The Beatles' first songs in the Liverpool council house with John Lennon.
body: A key to Sir Paul McCartney's childhood home has sold for thousands of pounds at auction.
During the 1950s and 60s, Sir Paul lived with his family at 20 Forthlin Road in Allerton, Liverpool, and composed some of the earliest Beatles' tracks with John Lennon there.

Sir Paul moved out in 1963, and his father and brother in the following year. In 1965, American superfan Kathy Salt wrote to then-occupant Ashley Jones, who enclosed a photograph of the house and a key, with a tag attached, in his letter back.
The three items were sold to a British private collector at Dominic Winter Auctioneers in the Cotswolds on Wednesday, fetching a hammer price of £5,000 - double the estimate.

articles.title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'
articles.summary: The Shaun of the Dead and Mission: Impossible films star had previously put symptoms down to "character fault".
body: Shaun of the Dead and Mission: Impossible films star Simon Pegg has revealed he has been diagnosed with ADHD, which he said "confirmed a lot of stuff that I'd been wrestling with".
Pegg, 56, who also co-created and starred in films Hot Fuzz, The World's End, and TV series Spaced, said "there was a lot of build-up and suspicion, and it just took a while actually to get there."
Speaking on the podcast I'm ADHD! No You're Not, external on Thursday, he said he pursued a diagnosis as he "just wanted to know".
ADHD symptoms focus on three main areas - inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity plus lack of concentration.

articles.title: The Hollywood Reporter Honors ‘The Koreans’ Star Han Ji-min With Trailblazer Award at Busan Gala
articles.summary: Studio executives, 'Bedford Park' star Moon Choi and 'KPop Demon Hunters' producer Agnes Lee were among the guests at THR and the Motion Picture Association’s American Film Night, celebrating creative ties between Hollywood and Korea.
body: Korean star Han Ji-min accepted The Hollywood Reporter ’s Trailblazer Award at a glitzy gala high above Busan on Wednesday night, promising that her creative journey was only just beginning.

The award was presented during American Film Night, a collaboration between THR and the Motion Picture Association (MPA), staged on the 33rd floor of the Park Hyatt Busan with sweeping views of the waterfront and Gwangan Bridge.

“I really enjoyed watching the original drama, so I was looking forward to seeing how it would change in a new Korean style, and it was a very meaningful time for me to be able to take part in that process. This is also a new challenge for me, so please look forward to it.”

With the 31st Busan International Film Festival entering its second night, an array of international industry figures took time away from the films and fanfare to honor Han and her two-decade career across television and film.

articles.title: How boxing inspired a play about men's mental health
articles.summary: The play explores losing a sense of purpose, the difficulty some men have talking about their mental health and the support they can find in each other.
body: For many athletes, years of training can provide a routine, a purpose and an identity - but what happens when it all stops?
That question is at the heart of a new play which explores men's mental health through the world of boxing.
The Corner Man follows a fighter forced to confront life outside the ring after spending years dedicated to the sport.
Writer and producer Cathal J Ferris said the idea grew from his own experience of boxing and conversations with fighters.

articles.title: BBC to cut raft of Radio 4 programmes including You and Yours
articles.summary: The corporation said it would be investing in a new consumer programme, while announcing more cuts.
body: The BBC has announced it will be cutting a raft of Radio 4 programmes including the long-running consumer and social affairs show You and Yours.
The social sciences show Thinking Allowed will also be cut along with arts and ideas programme Free Thinking, as the corporation seeks £500m savings.
Other shows such The Artificial Human and Open Country will also go, it was announced on Thursday, while Radio 5 Live will also see a reduction in commissioning on its schedule and podcasts.
The BBC has committed to investing in a new consumer programme, though, and two new weekly shows exploring ideas shaping the world, and the impact of technology and AI.
